name: Labor force participation, women 16 and over
plain: Out of every 100 women aged 16 and over who live in the area, how many are working or looking for work, as the survey estimates it.
definition: Women 16 and over in the labor force (employed, or unemployed: without work, looking for it and available), civilian or in the Armed Forces, divided by all women 16 and over, in percent (ACS B23001). This is the definition of ACS table S2301, which counts the Armed Forces in the labor force.
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the island value is the Census Bureau's own island row)

coverage.frequency: Three five-year windows that share no year: 2010-2014, 2015-2019 and 2020-2024, labelled 2014, 2019 and 2024. Because they do not overlap, a change from one to the next can be read and tested against its margin. The next window that shares no year with these is 2025-2029; women_labor.py adds a window only when its list of windows names it.

method: women_labor.py reads ACS 5-year table B23001 (Sex by Age by Employment Status for the Population 16 Years and Over) for each window: the per-sequence summary files for 2010-2014 and 2015-2019 and the table-based files for 2020-2024. For each sex it adds the cells of seven age groups (16-19, 20-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65 and over) into four counts: population, labor force (civilian and Armed Forces), civilian labor force and unemployed. The margin of a sum is the square root of the sum of the squared margins of its cells (a cell the Census Bureau controls to its own estimate has no printed margin and adds none). The rate is the women's labor force over the women's population, both summed over the seven age groups, and its margin follows the Census Bureau's formula for a proportion (ACS General Handbook, chapter 8). The value for a group of municipios is pooled: summed counts over summed counts, never an average of the municipio rates.
source_detail: ACS 5-year table B23001, cells 001-173 (males from 003, females from 089), vintages 2014 and 2019 (per-sequence files, 5_year_seq_by_state/PuertoRico) and 2024 (table-based file acsdt5y2024-b23001.dat), https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/
how_to_read: In 2020-2024, 41.9% (± 0.3 points) of the women 16 and over of Puerto Rico were in the labor force, against 51.4% (± 0.3) of the men; the women's rate was 40.4% in 2010-2014 and 39.8% in 2015-2019. Among the municipios it runs from 26.7% (± 5.7) in Maricao to 51.8% (± 2.3) in Trujillo Alto, leaving aside Culebra (64.0% ± 10.4), whose margin is too wide to rank. The rate counts every woman 16 and over, retired women included, so a municipio with an older population has a lower rate for that reason alone; the 25-to-54 rate (labor_sex.lfpr_women_prime) and the age-adjusted rate of the Knowledge Area page take that out.
caveats: A survey estimate, not a count: every value has a 90% margin of error (the Analysis tab shows it); two areas differ significantly only when the difference is larger than its own margin.
Small municipios have wide margins: in 2020-2024 Culebra's women's rate is 64.0% ± 10.4 points and Vieques's 38.6% ± 10.3, so neither can be ranked against most others.

The three windows share no year, so they can be compared with each other; do not set them beside the ACS 5-year windows that overlap them (2016-2020 to 2019-2023, for example), which share years with them.

name: Women in the labor force: counts by sex and age, by municipio and region (Knowledge Area data)
plain: The survey counts behind the Women in the labor force page: for Puerto Rico and each municipio, how many women and men of each age group live there, are in the labor force and are unemployed, with margins of error, so the rate of any group of municipios can be worked out.
definition: women_labor.json holds, under areas.<window> (2014, 2019 and 2024, for 2010-2014, 2015-2019 and 2020-2024) and keyed by GEOID (72 for Puerto Rico and the 78 municipios), for each sex (m, f) and the seven age groups of ages (16-19 to 65 and over), four counts in the order of cells: pop (population), lf (labor force, civilian and Armed Forces), clf (civilian labor force) and une (unemployed), each as [estimate, 90% margin]; kids: the women 20 to 64 and those in the labor force by age of own children (u6: with a child under 6; 617: children 6 to 17 only; none), from B23003; sample: the survey's unweighted people and housing units (2020-2024 only, B98003 and B98001). groups lists the 15 municipios of the Eastern Region of FPR's Eastern Region Strategic Vision (ersv) and the seven tourism regions; names gives each municipio's name. analysis.ersv holds, for each window, the region's measures (pooled rates with margins), those of the rest of the island and of Puerto Rico, the differences with the rest of the island and whether each is significant at 90%, the gender gaps, the age-adjusted rate with its Kitagawa split and the unweighted mean of the 15 municipio rates, and the change from 2010-2014 to 2020-2024.
geography: Puerto Rico, the 78 municipalities, and any group of them (the Eastern Region of the ERSV and the seven tourism regions are listed)

coverage.frequency: Three five-year windows that share no year: 2010-2014, 2015-2019 and 2020-2024, labelled 2014, 2019 and 2024. Because they do not overlap, a change from one to the next can be read and tested against its margin. The next window that shares no year with these is 2025-2029; women_labor.py adds a window only when its list of windows names it.

method: women_labor.py reads ACS 5-year table B23001 (Sex by Age by Employment Status for the Population 16 Years and Over) for each window: the per-sequence summary files for 2010-2014 and 2015-2019 and the table-based files for 2020-2024. For each sex it adds the cells of seven age groups (16-19, 20-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65 and over) into four counts: population, labor force (civilian and Armed Forces), civilian labor force and unemployed. The margin of a sum is the square root of the sum of the squared margins of its cells (a cell the Census Bureau controls to its own estimate has no printed margin and adds none). B23003 (Presence of Own Children Under 18 Years by Age of Own Children by Employment Status for Females 20 to 64 Years) is read the same way. A group's counts are the sums of its municipios' counts (margins added in quadrature) and its rates are pooled: summed labor force over summed population, never an average of rates. A region is compared with the rest of the island, not with the island total that contains it. A difference is significant when it is larger than its own 90% margin. The age-adjusted rate applies the region's rate in each age group to the age mix of the women 16 and over in the rest of the island (direct standardization); the gap with the rest of the island splits into a part due to the age mix and a part due to the rates within each age group (Kitagawa, 1955). The method is in women_labor.py and docs/analysis/women-labor-2026-10/README.md.
source_detail: ACS 5-year tables B23001 and B23003 (every window) and B98003 and B98001 (2020-2024), https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/
how_to_read: In 2020-2024 the 15 municipios of the Eastern Region had 183,952 women 16 and over (± 1,752), and 42.0% (± 0.8 points) of them were in the labor force, against 41.9% for the rest of the island: a difference of 0.1 points with a margin of ± 0.9, so not significant. Adjusted to the age mix of the rest of the island, the region's rate is 40.7%: the region's women are slightly younger, which raises its unadjusted rate by 1.3 points, while lower participation at 55 and over lowers it by 1.2 points in total. The plain average of the 15 municipio rates, 42.6%, gives Culebra the same weight as Humacao; the pooled rate is the region's own. From 2010-2014 to 2020-2024 the region's women's rate rose 1.3 points (± 1.1), a significant change, and its rate for women 25 to 54 rose 7.8 points (± 1.9).
caveats: A survey estimate, not a count: every value has a 90% margin of error (the Analysis tab shows it); two areas differ significantly only when the difference is larger than its own margin.
Small municipios have wide margins: in 2020-2024 Culebra's women's rate is 64.0% ± 10.4 points and Vieques's 38.6% ± 10.3, so neither can be ranked against most others.

The three windows share no year, so they can be compared with each other; do not set them beside the ACS 5-year windows that overlap them (2016-2020 to 2019-2023, for example), which share years with them.
The margin of a sum of municipios treats their estimates as independent, as the Census Bureau's approximation does; it is an approximation.
The survey's sample (the people and homes it interviewed) is published for 2020-2024 only: in the Eastern Region, 16,930 people and 10,139 housing units.
